notes: §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR1: "Debugging section(s), if specified, must appear together immediately after the DECLARATIVES header." ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclCollectSection sets _nonDebuggingDeclarativeSeen for every declarative section that is not a compiled debugging section and refuses (COBOL6948) a USE FOR DEBUGGING section collected after one; without WITH DEBUGGING MODE the section is skipped as comment lines (§1985:XV.2.1.3 GR2), so the rule applies only where the sections are compiled. The witness puts a debugging section after a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR section. Probes at --std 85: D,U,D refuses the second D; D,D,U compiles and runs (failed OPEN and the READ after it run the error USE, the debugging sections fire); U,D with zero paragraphs, U(INPUT),U(F2),D and a 2002 EC-I-O section before D all refuse (the EC form also draws COBOL0877/0878); U,D without DEBUGGING MODE compiles; nested programs keep the fact per program (outer U then a contained program's D first compiles). Read 6 (2026-11-14, records-read6): the row had no verdict and no test-ref although its witness existed; the reader read CONFORMS and an independent refuter UPHELD it (op-20261114/out-read6/rd-NN.json and rd-NN-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Debugging section(s), if specified, must appear together immediately after the DECLARATIVES header."; 2023: "No USE FOR DEBUGGING: the 2023 USE rules cover only AFTER EXCEPTION, BEFORE REPORTING, EC and EO forms; the Debug feature is dropped". No 2023 clause holds the Debug feature. The USE statement candidates never mention debugging sections or their placement, so the 1985 grouping requirement is dropped.
